title: COPY callback: HMAC devCtx not guarded — aliased Crypto2DevHmacCtx double-free
description:
wc_HmacCopy (hmac.c:341-359) does XMEMCPY(dst, src, sizeof(*dst)) directly — it does NOT dispatch through CryptoCb COPY at all. The COPY handler in wc_crypto2dev_cb cannot intercept this. However the aliasing is still real: after XMEMCPY, dst->devCtx == src->devCtx (same Crypto2DevHmacCtx*, same data buffer pointer, same key bytes). When either object is freed or finalized, ForceZero+XFREE runs on the shared block; the other then holds dangling pointers — use-after-free, double-free, key material readable in the second object's stale devCtx.

Fix direction (revised after qsi.11 research): the COPY handler guard originally proposed will NOT work since wolfSSL never calls it for HMAC copy. The correct fix options are:
(a) UPSTREAM: add CryptoCb COPY dispatch to wc_HmacCopy in wolfSSL, similar to wc_Sha256Copy. Until then the port cannot intercept.
(b) DOCUMENT: add a header warning that wc_HmacCopy is unsafe when devCtx is set; recommend not calling wc_HmacCopy on hardware-bound HMAC objects.
(c) WORKAROUND: on the devCtx callback, detect a stale devCtx by storing the owning hmac* in the Crypto2DevHmacCtx and asserting it matches — aborts rather than silent corruption.

Since wc_HmacCopy is not called internally by wolfSSL for TLS (only hash objects are copied for transcript), practical risk is application code that explicitly calls wc_HmacCopy on a hardware-bound HMAC. Priority downgraded P1→P2 pending upstream dispatch support.
